primary_question: Does controlled separation produce a clinically meaningful increase in target-tissue exposure over CereVasc's current delivery architecture, without compromising drainage or ICP?
comparator: CereVasc's CURRENT delivery (US11850390B2) — NOT generic lumbar puncture. CereVasc has demonstrated ovine CNS biodistribution via eShunt.

design.group_A: CereVasc baseline delivery (endovascular, no separation, no retention)
design.drug: FITC-dextran 150 kDa (bevacizumab surrogate) + separate cohort with scAAV9 (CereVasc has published biodistribution data)
design.sampling: CSF: 0,0.5,1,2,4,8,12,24,48h; Tissue: post-mortem; Venous: same; ICP: continuous; Drainage: continuous

endpoints.primary: Target-tissue AUC (brain-adjacent tissue drug concentration × time)
secondary: Time above evidence-backed PD target (where one exists for the selected agent)

success_threshold.primary: Group B tissue AUC ≥ 120% of Group A (conservative; model predicts 327%)
success_threshold.direction: Any improvement in correct direction supports the mechanism
success_threshold.safety: ICP < 20 mmHg; drainage ≥ 0.3 mL/min in both groups
success_threshold.pk_proxy_acknowledgment: If tissue concentration does not reach agent-specific PD target, result is relative exposure improvement (PK proxy), not therapeutic benefit

decision_tree.AUC ≥ 200% AND drainage safe: BUYABLE CONFIRMED — proceed to patent filing + partnership discussions
decision_tree.AUC 120-200% AND drainage safe: MILESTONE-WORTHY — improvement confirmed, magnitude smaller than model; recalibrate and reassess
decision_tree.AUC ≤ 120%: TRUE CEILING — model overestimated in vivo

commercial_context: CereVasc has already demonstrated ovine CNS biodistribution using eShunt. This experiment directly compares against their EXISTING delivery method — the most commercially meaningful comparison possible.
